top_buys.pitch: Fox just closed its $22B Roku deal, turning a legacy broadcaster into a streaming distribution owner.
top_buys.why: The acquisition completed today, so Fox now owns a large connected-TV platform with direct ad inventory and user data. Communication Services is the strongest sector of the past week, which gives the story a tailwind. Deal-closing news is usually underappreciated versus deal-announcement news, and the integration narrative can unfold over weeks.
top_buys.risks: A $22B purchase adds leverage and integration risk, and Roku's own margins are thin, so skeptics may push the stock lower first.
top_buys.watch: Fox's next earnings call for the first commentary on Roku's contribution and cost synergies.

top_buys.pitch: Falling crude and a looming glut squeeze oilfield service activity first.
top_buys.why: Brent's biggest weekly drop since 2020 plus reports of an emerging supply glut typically push producers to trim 2027 capex. Service companies like Halliburton see that in pricing and rig counts well before the integrated majors feel it. Energy is already the weakest sector of the week, down 11%, and that trend can persist as budget revisions come through.
top_buys.risks: Oil is heavily geopolitically driven, and any Iran escalation could spike crude and reverse this quickly; the stock is already beaten down.
top_buys.watch: North American rig counts and any producer capex guidance cuts in coming weeks.

top_buys.pitch: Rotation out of tech into steady, capital-returning banks is quietly working.
top_buys.why: Financials are up 1.8% over the past week while Technology fell 7.7%, and commentators are advising buying consistent dividend payers during the sell-off. A strong October jobs report reduces recession fear, which supports bank credit and fee income. Northern Trust is a lower-volatility way to play that rotation without chasing a headline.
top_buys.risks: If the correction broadens into a general risk-off move, banks fall too; and lower rates would compress net interest income.
top_buys.watch: Next week's inflation data and whether the rotation into financials continues.

top_buys.pitch: Same Roku-deal thesis via the cheaper voting-light share class.
top_buys.why: Fox completed its $22B Roku acquisition, giving it owned streaming distribution at a time when Communication Services is leading the market. The B shares often trade at a discount and track the same fundamentals.
top_buys.risks: Lower liquidity than FOXA and the same integration and leverage risks from a large acquisition.
top_buys.watch: Fox's next quarterly report for Roku integration details.

top_buys.pitch: A potential Häagen-Dazs international sale would unlock cash in a defensive name.
top_buys.why: The WSJ reports General Mills is evaluating a sale of its Häagen-Dazs business outside North America, which could fund debt paydown or buybacks. Consumer Staples is modestly positive while tech sells off, so defensive names get flows. Divestiture stories usually unfold over months rather than being fully priced on day one.
top_buys.risks: The sale may never happen, and General Mills' underlying volume trends remain weak.
top_buys.watch: Any confirmation of a sale process or buyer interest.
